# Hormuz Crisis and Building a Watch List

Report 185 | Published 2026-03-29 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2026-3-29/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/185.json)

Energy disruption and a selective watch list.

The shift toward prolonged-shock risk is justified, but the report overstates the global oil/gas share actually lost. Several watch-list names subsequently rebounded; those are useful observations, not claimed portfolio entries. Its strongest discipline is separating a valuation candidate from a purchase trigger and rejecting a single-episode safe-haven narrative.

**Coverage:** Full numbered text and image inventory read. All material theses across macro, digital assets, investment analysis and concluding sections considered. Position listings and incidental descriptive statistics are excluded unless they support a thesis.

## Claims

### 185-C01

**One-fifth of global gas disappeared.**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Wrong |
| Type | empirical |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | hormuz-supply-magnitude |
| Source blocks | 8 |
| Thesis family | hormuz-supply-magnitude |

The gas denominator is incorrect: IEA’s roughly 20% figure concerns LNG, which is a subset of total natural gas. The adjacent oil statement is less clear-cut: blocked chokepoint export flows are not the same as net world production lost. IEA’s March 12 projection of an 8mb/d net oil supply decline predates the article and is a forecast, not a final observed March result. The gas error should not be used to dismiss the severity of the oil-flow disruption.

**Direction:** See assessment; evidence is limited to the stated proposition.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Price direction alone does not identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [March 2026 oil market report](https://www.iea.org/reports/oil-market-report-march-2026) | IEA | 2026-03-12 | Verified in the audit

IEA projected an 8mb/d March global supply decline, with offsets from other regions and emergency reserve releases; chokepoint throughput is not identical to net global supply lost.

- [Global LNG disruption](https://www.iea.org/news/middle-east-crisis-disrupts-international-natural-gas-markets-and-delays-global-lng-supply-wave) | IEA | 2026-04-24 | Verified in the audit

Close to 20% of LNG supply was disrupted; LNG is a subset of natural gas. March global LNG production was 8% lower year over year after offsets elsewhere.

### 185-C15

**Low-growth businesses can reward cheap entry.**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Right |

| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |

| Thesis family | no-growth-value |

Positive distributable cash flow can produce a positive investor return without growth if the purchase price is low enough and the cash flow persists. The tobacco analogy does not prove alcohol demand or payout safety follows the same path.

**Direction:** See assessment; evidence is limited to the stated proposition.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Price direction alone does not identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Deductive assessment:**

- Cash flow persists
- Distributions reach shareholders
- No offsetting dilution or terminal loss

For a perpetuity with annual distributable cash C and required return r, value is C/r even at zero growth. Paying less raises the cash yield, conditional on persistence.

**Outcome evidence:**

No independent outcome source is recorded. Any deductive assessment is identified separately.

## Framework lessons

- Separate valuation from entry conditions.

## Verification limitations

- Current page snapshot is not an authenticated publication-date version.
- A missing horizon is not replaced with an invented author deadline.
- Market sensitivities use vendor adjusted closes and do not reconstruct portfolio execution.
